title: Weak equivalence of fibers transports along an edge for Kan fibrations
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns, geometric realization and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $S,Y_0,Y_1$ be simplicial sets and $p_i:Y_i\to S$ for $i=0,1$ be Kan fibrations, meaning that they lift every horn inclusion $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq j\leq n$. Let $m:Y_0\to Y_1$ satisfy $p_1m=p_0$, and let $e:\Delta^1\to S$ be an edge with endpoints $s_0=e(0)$ and $s_1=e(1)$. Put $T_i=\Delta^1\times_SY_i$ and $(Y_i)_{s_a}=\{s_a\}\times_SY_i$ for $i,a\in\{0,1\}$. For each $i,a$, the endpoint inclusion
$$(Y_i)_{s_a}\longrightarrow T_i,\qquad y\longmapsto(a,y)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently the induced strict-fiber map $m_{s_0}:(Y_0)_{s_0}\to(Y_1)_{s_0}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $m_{s_1}:(Y_0)_{s_1}\to(Y_1)_{s_1}$ is; each is also equivalent to the induced map $T_0\to T_1$ being a weak homotopy equivalence. No Kan hypothesis on $S$, $Y_0$ or $Y_1$, and no nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis, is imposed.

proof.text: For each i, pull back the Kan fibration p_i along the edge e to obtain q_i:T_i=Delta^1 x_S Y_i \to Delta^1. Horn lifting is preserved by pullback, so q_i is a Kan fibration even though S and Y_i need not be Kan. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], |q_i|:|T_i| \to |Delta^1| is a Serre fibration. The finite-limit and naturality assertion of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies |T_i| with the k-space pullback |Delta^1| x_{|S|} |Y_i| and identifies the realization of each strict endpoint fiber with the corresponding fiber of |q_i| over 0 or 1. Thus the maps in the first assertion are precisely the endpoint-fiber inclusions for these Serre fibrations.

proof.text: Let q:E \to |Delta^1| be one of these Serre fibrations and F_a=q^{-1}(a). If E is empty, F_a is empty and F_a \to E is a weak homotopy equivalence by the component-and-based-group definition. Otherwise choose x in E. Lift a path in the interval from q(x) to a; path lifting in [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] gives a point of F_a, so every endpoint fiber is nonempty. The same node gives the exact sequence and path-transport action. Since the interval is contractible, its positive homotopy groups and fundamental group vanish. For every point y in F_a, apply that exact sequence with base point y and base point a in the interval. Exactness therefore makes pi_n(F_a,y) \to pi_n(E,y) an isomorphism for every n>=1. This checks every base point in the source fiber, rather than using the previously chosen x, which need not belong to F_a. At degree zero, path lifting makes the map on fiber components surjective, while the orbit description in the cited statement has orbit set equal to the components of E and the acting fundamental group is trivial; hence it is injective as well. This proves F_a \to E is a weak equivalence for a=0,1, including disconnected total spaces and empty cases. By the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the corresponding simplicial endpoint inclusions are weak homotopy equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.16 and Proposition 2.4.18, printed pp. 55-57, for the Serre exact sequence, path lifting and component action; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The map m over S induces a map of pullbacks M:T_0 \to T_1 and, for each endpoint a, a commutative square of strict fibers and total pullbacks. Realization preserves this square by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. The vertical endpoint maps in the square are weak equivalences by Steps 1-2. The class of realized weak equivalences satisfies two-out-of-three by [lem-coef-topological-serre-model], so the horizontal fiber map m_{s_a} is a weak equivalence exactly when M is. Applying this for a=0 and a=1 proves the stated equivalence between the two strict-fiber maps and the induced map T_0 \to T_1. No property of S beyond the given edge, and no nonemptiness or connectedness assumption, entered the argument.

lean.statement: theorem kan_fibration_edge_fiber_transport {Y₀ Y₁ S : SSet.{u}} (p₀ : Y₀ ⟶ S) (p₁ : Y₁ ⟶ S) (m : Y₀ ⟶ Y₁) (hm : m ≫ p₁ = p₀) (hp₀ : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (j : Fin (n + 1)), HasLiftingProperty (SSet.horn n j).ι p₀) (hp₁ : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (j : Fin (n + 1)), HasLiftingProperty (SSet.horn n j).ι p₁) (e : Δ[1] ⟶ S) : (∀ (a : Fin 2), IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanEndpointInclusion p₀ e a) ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanEndpointInclusion p₁ e a)) ∧ (IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanStrictFiberMap p₀ p₁ m hm (kanEdgeEndpoint e 0)) ↔ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanStrictFiberMap p₀ p₁ m hm (kanEdgeEndpoint e 1))) ∧ (IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanStrictFiberMap p₀ p₁ m hm (kanEdgeEndpoint e 0)) ↔ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanEdgePullbackMap p₀ p₁ m hm e)) ∧ (IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanStrictFiberMap p₀ p₁ m hm (kanEdgeEndpoint e 1)) ↔ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (kanEdgePullbackMap p₀ p₁ m hm e))
